questions.stem: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
questions.explanation: INC founded 28 December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay. Founded by Allan Octavian Hume; first president W. C. Bonnerjee; 72 delegates.

questions.stem: The REVOLT OF 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at which cantonment town?
questions.explanation: Meerut — sepoys of the 3rd Bengal Light Cavalry refused greased cartridges; mutinied on 10 May 1857. Mangal Pandey's isolated act at Barrackpore was on 29 March 1857 (earlier). Delhi fell to mutineers the next day — Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed Emperor.

questions.stem: Match the COMMISSION / PLAN with its YEAR. A. Simon Commission. B. Nehru Report. C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact. D. Communal Award. List-II: 1. 1927. 2. 1928. 3. 1931. 4. 1932.
questions.explanation: Simon Commission 1927. Nehru Report (by Motilal Nehru) 1928. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 5 March 1931. Communal Award (Ramsay MacDonald) August 1932 → Poona Pact follows.

questions.stem: Consider the following about the INDIAN NATIONAL ARMY (INA / Azad Hind Fauj). 1. First organised by Mohan Singh in 1942 with Indian POWs of the Japanese. 2. Subhas Chandra Bose took over leadership in 1943 at Singapore. 3. The Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) declared war on Britain and the USA in October 1943. 4. The Red Fort trials (1945-46) of INA officers galvanised Indian public opinion against the British. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. First INA (Mohan Singh) formed 1942 but collapsed mid-1942 over command disputes. Bose took over in July 1943 (Singapore). Azad Hind Provisional Government established 21 Oct 1943; declared war on USA and Britain the next day. Red Fort trials of Shah Nawaz Khan, P. K. Sahgal, G. S. Dhillon in 1945-46 were a major nationalist rallying point.

questions.stem: Which viceroy is associated with the PARTITION OF BENGAL in 1905?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal along religious lines in October 1905 — widely seen as 'divide and rule'. Sparked the Swadeshi movement. Partition REVOKED in 1911 by Lord Hardinge II, same year Delhi became capital.

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims. REASON (R): The British sought to communalise Indian politics by giving distinct legislative representation to religious groups.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto) introduced SEPARATE electorates where Muslims could only be elected by Muslims, etc. Historians see this as a cornerstone of the 'divide and rule' strategy — eventually feeding into the two-nation theory. R correctly identifies the causal intent.
